title: The Goldkette band breaks up and Whiteman's offer
summary: Goldkette's men could not get bookings; Whiteman told them to join him, and Challis was told to come to the Paramount on September 20.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: He came in and he saw this, even wanted to know who did that. He was upset, but at least he could see for him we didn't mean any harm. We were just trying to make Paul feel good. So the guys, I guess, they went all around Atlantic City, and then Paul came up in the musician's room which was upstairs and we got talking. What are you guys going to do? -- actually what they heard was that the band was going to break up.

See, they couldn't get -- Jean couldn't book the band; O'Keefe couldn't book the band. Horvath couldn't book the band; and they wound up trying to book it in New York, at a place called the New York Club. So Paul had told the guys, he said, 'Well, I'd turn down that job. I don't think it will last ten days.' Anyway, what the guys were going to do they didn't know. They were mulling it over, trying to figure out what they should do and he said, 'Well, any of you guys could come with me, whenever you want.'

Now, Paul had a contract for 44 weeks a year for four or five years, but it was in theatres and then he had a European trip scheduled and then he had his recordings, and let's see, there was something else, recordings and then he

had whatever he could fill in with dance tours and concerts, so here's a guy's not worrying. The Goldkette organization is worried because they can't book the band. It's not any particular guy's fault. It's just that there were very few bands being booked anywhere. The business was bad for them. So what happened with the Goldkette band they had nothing to look forward to but to break up. They didn't know where they were going after Atlantic City.

However, Jean comes down and he has the Roseland booked for two weeks, at which time they want to make some records again. But that was the only thing they had to look forward to. Well, I jumped at the opportunity -- I said, 'I'd like to go.' 'Well, that's okay, you can come along on the 20th of September. Just be at the Paramount and we'll -- we go out from there. We go to Boston, and go to Boston with them.
